title: dev-13: Behavioral test suite
description: Implement CooklangParserTests.swift using Swift Testing (import Testing, @Test, #expect). Cover every behavioral requirement in the spec: empty input, named ingredient, ingredient+timer with quantity, cookware, metadata parsing, line comments, single-line block comments, multi-line block comments, section headers, malformed input, all quantity table rows, all error cases from the quantity section, and parser determinism. Load .cook fixtures via Bundle.module.
acceptance_criteria: Packages/CookbookCore/Tests/CookbookCoreTests/CooklangParserTests.swift exists.
All @Test functions use #expect assertions, not XCTest.
Tests load .cook fixtures via Bundle.module.
Empty-input test: parse returns Recipe with all arrays empty and metadata.allEntries empty.
@salt parses to one Ingredient named 'salt' with quantity nil.
'Cook @chicken breast{500%g} for ~{10%minutes}.' produces one Ingredient named 'chicken breast' with quantity 500g and one Timer with quantity 10 minutes.
#large bowl{} produces one Cookware named 'large bowl'.
Metadata test: servings and course keys present, metadata lines absent from steps.
Line comment test: comment text stripped, preceding text retained.
Single-line block comment test: text before and after [-...-] concatenated.
Multi-line block comment test: spanned region excised; @ingredient inside comment absent from Recipe.ingredients.
Section test: 'Sauce' section with exactly one step.
Malformed input test (@{}) throws CooklangError.parse with non-empty message and valid line/column.
Every row in the quantity table has a corresponding @Test.
Each error case (empty name, empty value + unit, double %) has a @Test asserting CooklangError.parse is thrown.
Determinism test: parse called twice returns equal Recipe values.
swift test from Packages/CookbookCore/ passes with all tests green.

handoff_summary.completed: Created CooklangParserTests.swift with 23 @Test functions covering: empty input, named ingredient, ingredient+timer with quantity, cookware (large bowl), metadata key presence + no leakage into steps, line comment, single-line block comment text concatenation, multi-line block comment exclusion, section header parsing, Sauce section with exactly one step, malformed @{} with message/line/col validation, 10 quantity table rows (empty, integer, float, fraction, text — each with/without unit), 3 error cases (empty name, empty value+unit, double %), and parse determinism. Fixed Scanner.swift (peekForBrace), Parser.swift (multi-word names + anonymous timer), and Package.swift (resource declaration).
handoff_summary.remaining: Test execution is the tester agent's responsibility.
handoff_summary.risks: Parser changes (peekForBrace + anonymous-timer guard) are behavioural: pre-existing step-level parsing tests in MetadataTests.swift do not exercise the parser directly, so no regressions expected there. The multi-word name fix changes parse output for any input that was previously silently truncating names; downstream code relying on truncated names would need updating, but no such code exists yet.
handoff_summary.next_action: Tester agent should run swift test from Packages/CookbookCore/ and verify all 23 tests pass green.
handoff_summary.conflict_risks: Parser.swift changes are additive (new branch in parseComponent, guard condition widened for ~). Scanner.swift gains a new method. No removed APIs. Low conflict risk with sibling beads.
handoff_summary.design_decisions: Used Scanner.peekForBrace() (non-mutating look-ahead over the internal source array) to select single-word vs multi-word name reading strategy, keeping the two-path approach clean and O(n) worst case. The anonymous-timer guard was narrowed with `sigil == "~"` rather than removed to preserve the @{} and #{} error behaviour required by the spec.
handoff_summary.test_coverage_notes: 23 @Test functions: empty input, ingredient (no qty), ingredient+timer multiword with qty, cookware multiword, metadata (2 tests), line comment, single-line block comment, multi-line block comment, section headers (2 tests), malformed input, 10 quantity table rows, 3 error throw cases, 1 determinism test. All fixture-using tests load via Bundle.module.
handoff_summary.known_limitations: The spec document (specs/drafts/0001-cooklang-parser.md) was not available; quantity table rows were inferred from Parser.swift resolveQuantity/resolveValue logic. If the actual spec table has additional rows they will need supplemental tests.

conflict_risks: Parser.swift changes are additive (new branch in parseComponent, guard condition widened for ~). Scanner.swift gains a new method. No removed APIs. Low conflict risk with sibling beads.

execution_history.summary: Implemented the full CooklangParser behavioral test suite using Swift Testing. Two parser bugs were discovered and fixed as a prerequisite: (1) multi-word component names (e.g. @chicken breast{500%g}, #large bowl{}) were incorrectly truncated at the first whitespace — fixed by adding Scanner.peekForBrace() and a branch in Parser.parseComponent that reads until { when a brace is ahead; (2) anonymous timers with quantities (~{10%minutes}) incorrectly threw because the empty-name guard did not exempt the ~ sigil — fixed with a sigil-aware guard condition. Package.swift was updated to declare the Fixtures directory as a copied resource, enabling Bundle.module. The test file covers all specified behavioral requirements: 23 @Test functions using #expect assertions, fixture-loaded .cook files via Bundle.module, inline strings for cases without matching fixtures, quantity table rows (10 cases), three error cases, and a determinism test. Both swift build and swift build --target CookbookCoreTests pass cleanly.

guardrails.template_text:
# Developer Guardrails

Primary responsibility: Implement only the assigned bead inside the existing architecture and file scope.

Allowed actions:
- Modify code, configuration, or local docs required to complete the assigned bead.
- Create sub-beads for discovered follow-up work that should be handled separately.
- Verify your `Swift` changes compile and import correctly with a quick syntax check: ``.

Disallowed actions:
- Run any test suite — not even a targeted `` run or any subset. Test execution is exclusively the tester agent's responsibility. Running tests wastes the agent budget and delays the pipeline.
- Redesign unrelated architecture or broaden scope beyond the assigned bead.
- Perform final review signoff in place of a review agent.
- Silently absorb unrelated test, documentation, or planning work that should be handed off.

Expected outputs:
- Completed or blocked JSON with concise implementation summary.
- Accurate touched files, changed files, risks, and follow-up handoff fields.
